# DotGame.Imaging

PNG, JPEG and WebP image codecs, with no dependencies: a decoder and an encoder for each.

[Documentation](../README.md)

## DotGame.Imaging

| Type | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [ImageDecoder](ImageDecoder.md) | class | Reads an image in any format this library decodes, telling which from its bytes: PNG ([`PngCodec`](PngCodec.md)), JPEG ([`JpegCodec`](JpegCodec.md)) and WebP ([`WebPCodec`](WebPCodec.md)) now, and any format added later, without a change to the code that calls it. |
| [PixelLayout](PixelLayout.md) | enum | How the pixels in a buffer are laid out: the order of their channels and the bytes each takes. |

## DotGame.Imaging.Jpeg

| Type | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [JpegCodec](JpegCodec.md) | class | Reads and writes JPEG images. |
| [JpegEncoderOptions](JpegEncoderOptions.md) | class | How [`JpegCodec.Encode`](JpegCodec.md#encode) writes an image: its defaults are cjpeg 3.2.1's, and with the same settings the file is byte for byte what cjpeg writes. |
| [JpegSubsampling](JpegSubsampling.md) | enum | How a JPEG image's chroma (its Cb and Cr components) is sampled against its luma, as cjpeg's `-sample` sets it. |

## DotGame.Imaging.Png

| Type | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [PngCodec](PngCodec.md) | class | Reads and writes PNG images: every color type and bit depth, palettes, transparency and interlacing when reading, 8 bits a sample when writing. |
| [PngCompressionLevel](PngCompressionLevel.md) | enum | How hard [`PngCodec.Encode`](PngCodec.md#encode) works to make a PNG file small: its members, and their order, are those of the runtime's `System.IO.Compression.CompressionLevel`. |

## DotGame.Imaging.WebP

| Type | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [WebPCodec](WebPCodec.md) | class | Reads and writes WebP images: lossy (VP8) with or without alpha, and lossless (VP8L). |
| [WebPEncoderOptions](WebPEncoderOptions.md) | class | How [`WebPCodec.Encode`](WebPCodec.md#encode) writes an image: its defaults are cwebp's, and with the same settings the file is byte for byte what cwebp 1.6.0 writes (lossless as `-lossless`, and so on). |
